title: Staging-local MariaDB 11.4 schema dump mutation guard repair

phases.objective: Ensure the disposable MariaDB 11.4 schema dump guard detects only top-level data-mutation statements and does not reject valid schema clauses such as ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.

e2e_journeys.actor: Governed CI and staging-local Windows migration operator
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Exact-SHA static validation followed by a freshly authorized disposable Windows Docker MariaDB 11.4 schema-only replay
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The builder produces authenticated role-specific schema-only dumps when the dump contains no top-level data-mutation statements, or fails closed before downstream automation.
steps: Run builder syntax, regression, plan, migration-governance, and environment-impact checks on the exact source head.
Classify dump statements after splitting SQL and removing leading comments so ON UPDATE clauses inside CREATE TABLE remain valid schema.
Run a fresh exact-SHA Windows preflight after any merged source change.
Run one freshly authorized disposable local Windows Docker MariaDB 11.4 schema-only replay and preserve stdout, stderr, evidence, and manifest.
Stop before AutoPilot, importer, readback, data export/import, deployment, provider, Hostinger, Cloudflare, or production operations.
assertions: mariadb-dump uses the same generated disposable root password as schema apply and table inspection.
The dump guard rejects top-level INSERT, REPLACE, UPDATE, DELETE, and LOAD DATA statements.
The dump guard does not reject ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP or other schema-only text inside CREATE TABLE.
The fix changes no immutable schema.sql and no published historical migration.
Static checks perform no database connection, database mutation, provider access, credential access, data export, or runtime mutation.
The Windows replay is limited to a disposable local MariaDB 11.4 schema-only build and fails closed on any error.
AutoPilot, importer, readback, production, provider, runtime, and credential actions remain forbidden.
